messages:
sam: handing off — quick follow-up from the INC-987 postmortem. two remediation items: (1) cache eviction race (PR #452) and (2) kube restartPolicy change for model-workers. PR 452 claims to address the eviction ordering and adds a small integration test. can someone verify the canary results?

maria: i merged PR 452 yesterday and kicked a canary to staging (link: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/452). deploy-bot shows rollout at 15% for the last 2 hours. i ran the smoke script once, looked ok.

jordan: any perf/regression metrics to watch? especially p50/p99 of token-latency and cache-hit-rate. if cache-hit drops we should rollback.

maria: good call. i'm watching these:
- metric: infra.cache.hit_rate (1m)
- metric: runtime.token_latency.p99
I posted a quick grafana panel snapshot: https://grafana.internal/d/mNQ4YV/canary-452

sam: that covers remediation 1, I think we can mark it closed in the postmortem tracker after one more 12h observation window. i'm going to add a follow-up card for automated synthetic that asserts the test-key survival.

sam: oncall ask: can @alex run the small evict verification on prod-canary and paste logs so we can close the remediation? steps are in the postmortem runbook: https://confluence.redwood/INC-987-runbook

alex: can do. i'm free in ~30m. what exact query do you want me to run?

maria: run this on the canary node: 
```bash
kubectl logs -n inference deploy/cache-worker-canary | grep -E "evict|cache miss" -A2 -B1 | tail -n 100
```
Look for consistent evict ordering and that the test key isn't evicted prematurely.

alex: running now... paste below when finished.

ops-bot: [automated] canary rollout status: cache-worker-canary: 15% -> 30% over last 45m, no error-rate increase detected (5m window).

alex: pasted logs: 
"2026-02-12T21:12:03Z cache-worker evict key=model_a_123
2026-02-12T21:12:03Z cache-worker set key=model_a_123 size=2KB
2026-02-12T21:12:04Z cache-worker miss key=model_b_456
2026-02-12T21:12:05Z cache-worker evict key=model_b_456"
Looks like ordering preserved, evictions correspond to expected LRU behavior. no premature evict on test key.

jordan: great. any anomalies in token-latency?

alex: quick check: token-latency.p99 for canary is stable: 210ms -> 215ms, within noise. cache.hit_rate steady at 0.82.

maria: remediation 2 (kube restartPolicy) hasn't been applied to prod yet — PR #459 still pending because infra team needs a config tweak. I assigned @jordan but you may need to coordinate with infra proper.

jordan: yes, i'll pick it up tomorrow AM and try to get the config merged by EOD. it's lower risk but important for controlled restarts.

sam: FYI I'll be oncall tonight 22:00-06:00 UTC. @alex can you cover my pager for 00:00-04:00? need a quick swap if possible.

alex: i can cover 00:00-04:00, no prob. leaving a note in the handoff doc.

maria: thanks both — small ask: if you see error spikes after 23:00 please escalate to the incident channel immediately; given the canary is still ramping. :exclamation: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [automated] alert: infra.cache.eviction_error rate increased 3x at 2026-02-12T23:14:02Z in prod-canary region.

sam: seeing ops-bot alert — pulling up logs. alex: if it persists during your cover, please open an incident and tag me.

alex: on it, pinging infra-sre. initial logs show a transient connection error to redis cluster, suspects network flaps. posting snippet: 
```
ERROR redis_conn: timeout connecting to redis: dial tcp 10.4.8.12:6379: i/o timeout
```

jordan: if that's true we should not flip the migration restarts until redis connection stability is verified. reopening postmortem item until infra confirms fix.

maria: reopening INC-987 remediation tracker item #2 for restartPolicy and adding secondary item: "verify redis network stability during canary ramp".

sam: acknowledged. i'm staying on until 23:30 then handing to alex. it'll be in the handoff notes.

alex: acknowledged, will escalate if alert persists.

maria: thanks all. i'll update the postmortem doc with the reopen and assign follow-ups. closing this thread for async coordination — ping here for any immediate handoff notes.

sam: thanks team :heart:
